title: Recognise 'cd <dir> && <test>' as a check and show which checks a checkpoint recognised
outcome:
Reported by Engram::Opus (session-7284, mailbox #192, 2026-09-25). It ran `cd /c/github/Personal/Engram && cargo test --lib 2>&1 | tail -n 3` through the Bash tool (1019 passed). Nothing was recorded. engram_check_command (engram_check_recognition.rs:39-64) reads only the line's first command, which was `cd`, so no check existed. That is by design from tm-winf step 2, but agents very often put a cd in front of their commands, and the miss is silent: the obligation just stays open, and it took a mailbox round trip to explain.

Proposed:
(1) Recognise `cd <literal dir> && <one test command>` as a check run in that directory. The directory must be a literal, resolved through the existing crediting rules (engram_literal_directory, network guard, leads-out rejection). Anything after the test still makes it non-simple, which means unknown.
(2) Make recognition visible: the checkpoint control card, or the turn's Engram card, lists the checks it recognised and each one's outcome (passed / unknown with a reason: masked exit, overlapped, outside the worktree, not finished). An agent can then see why a run didn't count without asking.

Not a bug in the evidence rules: a piped run like `| tail` is still correctly reported as unknown. See also tm-29gv (the PowerShell tool is not observed at all).
disposal_reason: Backlog triage w-930e4d333f07 (Architect1 batch 2, spot-checked by Termal::Fable2): CLOSE-DONE. Greg's "support little, but correctly" became the one-call `pushd "DIR" && TEST` form with not-reported notices (src/engram_check_recognition.rs:46-66).
